findings.statement: CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer_status ON orders (customer_id, status)
findings.title: Statement #2: Lock-sensitive DDL executes without an active `lock_timeout` in effect at this position
likely_causes: No SET lock_timeout was executed prior to this statement (or a prior SET LOCAL lock_timeout expired on COMMIT/ROLLBACK)
findings.recommendation: Configure `SET lock_timeout = '2s';` (or `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '2s';` inside the current transaction) BEFORE executing DDL.

findings.statement: CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer_status ON orders (customer_id, status)
findings.title: Statement #2: CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY acquires a SHARE lock that blocks all writes
likely_causes: Standard CREATE INDEX holds SHARE lock for the entire index build
findings.recommendation: Rewrite as CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY outside of a transaction block.

findings.statement: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_orders_concurrent_in_tx ON orders (created_at)
findings.title: Statement #3: CONCURRENTLY operation inside an open BEGIN transaction block will fail at runtime
likely_causes: PostgreSQL prohibits CONCURRENTLY index/partition operations inside explicit transaction blocks
findings.recommendation: Commit the preceding transaction (`COMMIT;`) before executing CONCURRENTLY statements, or move them to a non-transactional migration file.

findings.statement: ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN shipping_address SET NOT NULL

findings.statement: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE LOWER(customer_email) = 'alice@example.com' AND status = 'PAID' ORDER BY created_at DESC OFFSET 5000

likely_causes: Applying a function to a column prevents plain column B-Tree index lookups
findings.recommendation: Rewrite predicate as a range filter (for dates) or create an expression index on `(LOWER(customer_email))`.

findings.statement: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE LOWER(customer_email) = 'alice@example.com' AND status = 'PAID' ORDER BY created_at DESC OFFSET 5000
findings.title: Deep OFFSET pagination (OFFSET 5000) scans and discards 5000 rows on every query
likely_causes: PostgreSQL must materialize and skip all preceding rows to satisfy OFFSET
findings.recommendation: Replace OFFSET pagination with keyset (seek) pagination: `WHERE (created_at, id) < ($1, $2) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT N`.

findings.statement: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE LOWER(customer_email) = 'alice@example.com' AND status = 'PAID' ORDER BY created_at DESC OFFSET 5000
findings.title: Unbounded SELECT * fetches wide rows (including TOAST columns) and prevents Index-Only Scans
likely_causes: Fetching all columns forces heap page fetches even when filter columns are covered by an index
findings.recommendation: Project only required columns to enable Index-Only Scans and reduce network/TOAST I/O.

findings.statement: SELECT id, total_cents FROM orders WHERE notes ILIKE '%urgent%' AND created_at >= '2026-01-01'
findings.title: Leading wildcard LIKE/ILIKE ('%pattern') prevents standard B-Tree index usage

findings.recommendation: Enable pg_trgm extension and create a GIN trigram index: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_trgm ON table USING gin (col gin_trgm_ops);`

findings.statement: SELECT id FROM customers WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)
findings.title: NOT IN (SELECT ...) uses hashed/materialized subplan and returns 0 rows if any NULL exists in subquery

findings.recommendation: Rewrite `NOT IN (SELECT ...)` as `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ... WHERE ...)` for anti-join optimization and safe NULL semantics.
